title: Everyone Hated This Stock Now. The Market Got It Wrong
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; minor garbling around Meta Connect product details and some figures
summary: Couch Investor defends SoFi as 'the most hated retail stock' despite strong execution: YTD down ~40% but revenue +40%, net income +61%, members +35%, tangible book value/share +56%, deposits $45.5B, record $14.8B loan originations (+69%). He owns every share with zero plans to sell but issues no explicit buy directive — positive commentary only (SOFI, NU, HOOD, META all UNCERTAIN as calls). He stresses valuation (~$21B market cap, trailing P/E 34.4, forward ~22.6, PEG ~6) and that raised 2026 guidance (revenue, not EPS — a higher tax rate cost ~5 cents) came despite worse macro assumptions; Q3 commentary on Q4/2027 outlook will be the key sentiment event. Also covers Nu (-19% YTD): Q1 first $1B profit, revenue $5.9B (+39% FX-neutral), ROE 33%, ~140M customers; and Robinhood (+6% YTD): $1.3B revenue (+32%), transaction revenue +44%, saved by prediction markets offsetting the crypto drop. Macro section: 10-year at 5.1% (highest since 2007) with the S&P near all-time highs — a 'very weird situation,' not 2021/22 or dot-com. Meta Connect: Meta up 3.6%; Muse AI voice/video and glasses (including FDA-cleared hearing-aid glasses, Ray-Ban Gen 3, ~$1,200 VR glasses spring 2027, Muse charm). He says Meta without Muse should be above $800 and is still undervalued. Calls: none explicit.
